sources.title: Introducing the next generation of Claude
sources.evidence: March 4, 2024 announcement says Opus is available that day, identifies the Claude 3 family, and gives Opus a 200K standard context. It describes image understanding; 1M context was a special-use offering requiring inquiry.

sources.title: The Claude 3 Model Family: Opus, Sonnet, Haiku
sources.evidence: Indexed primary PDF text identifies Anthropic's Claude 3 Opus and confirms text/image inputs with text output and function calling. The indexed introduction includes the June 20, 2024 Sonnet 3.5 addendum. Direct full-document retrieval failed: web size limit (28,782,922 bytes), then HTTP 403 via local retrieval. No complete PDF inspection is claimed.

sources.title: Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models
sources.evidence: October 29, 2025 paper's Methods Notes explicitly include production Opus 3, separately distinguishing helpful-only variants. All experiments record/inject activations in layer residual streams. The discussion frames the studied systems as transformer-based language models. It supplies no model parameter counts or dense/MoE classification.

sources.title: Claude can now use tools
sources.evidence: May 30, 2024 announcement makes tool use generally available across the entire Claude 3 family on the Anthropic Messages API and partner platforms. It describes structured tool selection and forced tool use. It also announces thinking tags in Opus tool-use outputs; this is not the later configurable extended-thinking API mode.

sources.title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet System Card
sources.evidence: Accessible 43-page later card includes exact Claude 3 Opus columns in its comparison tables and discusses earlier Opus results. No parameter count is given. Section 1.2 introduces extended thinking for Claude 3.7 Sonnet, contradicting Google's retained 3.7 unsupported-thinking row.

sources.title: Partner model deprecations — Claude 3 Opus on Google Cloud
sources.evidence: Retained exact Opus section lists 200K input context, text/code/image inputs, text output, function calling, and no extended thinking. It gives May 31, 2024 provider launch and expired prospective shutdown wording. Generic PDF links and an 8K output limit require caution; the same page incorrectly labels 3.7 Sonnet extended thinking unsupported.

sources.title: Model deprecations
sources.evidence: Deprecation history maps the current display name Claude Opus 3 to exact API identifier claude-3-opus-20240229 and states its January 5, 2026 retirement.

sources.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
sources.evidence: Anthropic explicitly states that Claude model weights are not publicly released or customizable. This supports the closed-weight classification independently of hosted API availability; the evaluated Claude models in this later article are newer variants.

sources.title: Commercial Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Commercial service terms restrict reverse engineering and duplication, and reserve intellectual-property rights except where expressly granted. These establish proprietary service access, not an open model-weight redistribution license.

sources.title: An update on our model deprecation commitments for Claude Opus 3
sources.evidence: February 25, 2026 update confirms January 5 formal retirement but says Opus 3 remains available to paid claude.ai users and by request on the API. Thus retirement must not be described as universal unavailability. No endpoint request was tested in this audit.

sources.title: PDF support
sources.evidence: Current PDF documentation applies to active models and does not independently verify native PDF blocks for retired Opus 3. The exact Google provider Documents row is the narrower basis for a provider-supported file format.

sources.title: Claude 3 family model card with later addenda — complete accessible copy
sources.evidence: Parent retrieved and searched the full 64-page combined card. Exact Opus and Sonnet 3 comparisons report evaluation results, not total or active parameter counts. The original introduction establishes text/image inputs, text outputs and function calling; the context section distinguishes 200K production from 1M research contexts.

name.note: Anthropic's deprecation history uses this display name for the exact dated API identifier; the original branding was Claude 3 Opus.

developer.note: Developer identified in the original model card.

family.note: Catalog normalization of the explicitly named Claude 3 family.

release_date.note: First public availability is explicit in the dated announcement. The 20240229 identifier suffix is earlier; Google's May 31 date is provider availability.

open_weights.note: Anthropic explicitly keeps Claude weights nonpublic; Opus 3 preservation provides hosted access, not released weights.

license.note: Retain as the catalog's broad proprietary-service classification. This is not a named redistribution license for downloadable model weights.

parameters_b.note: No total count is disclosed in the inspected announcement, exact-model interpretability paper or later 3.7 comparison card. No third-party estimate is adopted. Parent also reviewed the full original card with later addenda from an accessible CDN copy.

active_parameters_b.note: No active parameter count or routing specification is reported. Active parameters cannot be inferred from Transformer structure.

architecture.note: Exact production Opus 3 is in the methods list; residual-stream interventions and the authors' transformer-based framing support generic Transformer structure. Dense versus MoE remains undisclosed; no feature-dictionary size is treated as parameters.

context_window.note: Standard public context in tokens. The launch footnote offers 1M for special use cases by inquiry, not as the generally available API limit.

modalities.note: Text/image-to-text is explicit in the original card. PDF is retained narrowly as a provider-documented input format from the exact Google Opus 3 Documents row, consistent with the catalog format taxonomy. That row does not prove native Anthropic PDF-block support or a current working endpoint.

reasoning.note: False refers to the dedicated extended-thinking mode introduced with Sonnet 3.7, corroborated by the exact Opus 3 provider table. Opus 3 tool-use thinking tags are ordinary prompted reasoning, not that later budgeted mode. This historical classification combines developer feature chronology with provider evidence; the provider table alone is unreliable for Sonnet 3.7.

tool_call.note: Claude 3 family tool use became generally available May 30, 2024; the exact retained Opus provider table independently lists function calling. This is a historical capability, not proof of current endpoint access.

description.value: Anthropic's Claude 3 Opus model accepts text and images and generates text, with a 200,000-token standard context and tool calling.
description.note: Replace the generic historical-release placeholder with documented capabilities, without performance superlatives.

patch.description: Anthropic's Claude 3 Opus model accepts text and images and generates text, with a 200,000-token standard context and tool calling.
patch.notes: Total and active parameter counts and dense/MoE classification remain undisclosed in the inspected evidence; generic Transformer structure is documented. Standard context is 200K; the launch offered 1M for specific uses by inquiry. Formal Anthropic API retirement was January 5, 2026, but the February 25 update documents continued paid claude.ai and by-request API access. No endpoint was tested. Dedicated extended thinking is distinct from the ordinary thinking tags documented for Opus 3 tool use. PDF is a provider-documented input format from Google; native Anthropic PDF-block support is not established. Proprietary denotes service access, not a model-weight redistribution license.

sources.label: Complete Claude 3 model card with later addenda

summary: All 14 fields reviewed. Add Transformer architecture, tool calling, false for dedicated extended thinking, provider-documented PDF input format and a concrete description. Confirm March 4 public release and 200K standard context. Counts remain undisclosed after full original and later-card inspection. Retain post-retirement hosted-access and provider-format caveats.
